summary: A Pt overlayer deposited on air-oxidized Nb films undergoes thermally driven reactions that form a Pt-rich Nb–Pt alloy (primarily NbPt$_3$) at the surface while dissolving the native oxide, as confirmed by VEXPS, EXAFS, TEM, and DFT. This encapsulation strategy preserves bulk superconducting properties ($T_c = 9.30 	imes 0.10$ K, RRR = 64) while protecting both planar surfaces and device sidewalls against re-oxidation, offering a scalable pathway to reduce TLS-induced decoherence in Nb transmon qubits.
motivation: Native Nb$_2$O$_5$, NbO$_2$, and NbO oxides are major sources of two-level system losses that limit coherence in superconducting transmon qubits. Existing in situ encapsulation methods cannot prevent oxidation of lithographically exposed sidewalls, which exhibit high electric-field participation and enhanced decoherence.
method: High-purity Nb films were grown epitaxially on c-plane sapphire at 700 °C (110 nm thick, $T_c = 9.30 \pm 0.10$ K), exposed to air to form (2.6 ± 0.2) nm native oxide, then capped with ~10 nm Pt and annealed at 750 °C for 2 hours. Multi-technique characterization (variable-energy XPS with 11 photon energies 2–5.5 keV, Pt L$_3$-edge EXAFS at grazing incidence, HAADF-STEM, EDX, and DFT) mapped oxide reduction and alloy formation.
result: Pt L$_3$-edge EXAFS fits to NbPt$_3$ with reduced $\chi^2 = 2.38$ and R-factor $5.6 \times 10^{-3}$, yielding Pt–Pt and Pt–Nb bond lengths of (2.756 ± 0.001) Å and (2.781 ± 0.003) Å. VEXPS shows Nb$^{5+}$ and Nb$^{4+}$ peaks shift 0.8 eV to lower binding energy post-annealing (indicating partial oxide reduction), while buried Alloy-1 (NbPt$_2$) and surface-dominant Alloy-2 (NbPt$_3$) form with depth-dependent fractions. DFT confirms Nb-to-Pt electron transfer creates an electric field that drives O$^{2-}$ diffusion into bulk and enables Nb–Pt intermixing with up to 0.7 eV/atom energy gain.
